facts.raw_span: a 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near her gluteal cleft
denied fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding
a 4 × 4 cm area of swelling just left of the natal cleft at the level of the tip of the coccyx
mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin but no fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits
no fluid was obtained
a complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass was excised from the subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx
the mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter
a high suspicion for abscess
the differential diagnosis at this time included inclusion cyst and soft-tissue tumor
percutaneous aspiration was performed in clinic
a 6-cm vertical incision was made over the lesion in the prone jack-knife position
the specimen was oriented with sutures and sent for permanent pathology
